summary:
SMART TREE — An Integrated Environmental Intelligence and Smart Air-Purification Concept

SMART TREE is an integrated environmental technology concept designed to connect Earth observation data, environmental intelligence, and sustainable air-quality solutions. It combines NASA Earth science resources, environmental monitoring architecture, and an interactive Digital Twin dashboard within a unified system.

The proposed design integrates multi-stage air filtration, a microalgae-based photobioreactor, solar-powered operation, and environmental sensing. Its digital architecture incorporates meteorological data from NASA POWER to support environmental analysis, temporal visualization, and the development of future AI-assisted predictive capabilities.

Aligned with the Be An Earth System Trend Detective! challenge, SMART TREE explores how Earth science data can be structured and visualized to better understand environmental conditions and their evolution over time, while connecting these insights to a practical sustainability-oriented application.

By bridging space-based environmental information with an innovative air-purification concept, SMART TREE presents a pathway toward more informed environmental monitoring and sustainable urban solutions. The current deliverable is a digital prototype and engineering concept; physical deployment, real-world sensor validation, and quantitative AI model evaluation remain future development stages.
details: SMART TREE is an integrated environmental technology concept that connects Earth observation data, environmental monitoring, and sustainable air-purification design. The proposed system combines a multi-stage air-filtration unit using HEPA and activated-carbon filters, a microalgae-based photobioreactor, solar-energy components, and environmental sensors. Its digital architecture includes a Digital Twin dashboard designed to organize, visualize, and interpret environmental information. For the Earth-data component, the project uses hourly meteorological data from NASA POWER for Tunis, Tunisia, covering January 1–7, 2026. These data provide environmental context for analysis and visualization; they are not presented as direct measurements of local PM2.5 or PM10 concentrations. The project was developed as a digital prototype using Python-based data processing and an interactive dashboard. It also explores how AI-assisted analysis could support future environmental prediction. The current version does not claim a validated predictive model, live sensor measurements, or physical deployment. SMART TREE is creative in combining space-based environmental information with a practical urban sustainability concept. Its intended impact is to encourage data-informed environmental awareness and provide a foundation for future testing and development.
